content:
Unified Folders A setting often used by people who have several mail accounts, but like to see an amalgamated list of eg: all emails in Inbox for all accounts in one unified folder.

Only the default folders display as unified folders. Inbox, Drafts, Templates, Sent. Archives, Spam, Trash

The Unified Inbox will have a chevron > to the left indicating it has separate accounts listed. > Inbox If you click on > then it expands to show the various separate mail account inboxes.

Scenario: If a Unified folder eg: Inbox is expanded and only has one account shown, then you may wish to add the Inbox of the other accounts.

  • Right click on Unified Inbox and select 'Properties'
  • Click on 'Choose' button
  • You can then see list of accounts and you need to select the checkboxes for 'Inbox' for all accounts including 'Local Folders'.
  • Click on 'OK'
  • Click on 'Update'

Same process for any Unified Folder - if 'Sent' then make sure you only select the 'Sent' folders of all the accounts.

re :The CFCC shows up in my Unified Folder list but the Gmail does not. Is that normal? Below the list of default Unified folders those you will see the separate names of your accounts. Those accounts display if they contain any folders you created or default folders that have not been selected to be displayed in Unified Folders. Local Folders being the last.

If the gmail account has no folders you created and all it's default folders are selected to display in Unified Folders then it has nothing to display, so will not display.

But you may have a gmail Inbox that has sub folders ? Do you want those subfolders to be displayed under that Inbox section in Unified Folders. If you check the 'Unified Inbox' for 'Properties' and click on 'Choose' - any Inbox subfolder may be selected - if you uncheck those subfolders, then they will be forced to display in a separate gmail account folder.

'All Folders' is the default display option which you have also chosen to be displayed. It shows all accounts one after the other and they all have their own set of folders.

content:
Not a bug, exactly, but a limitation of the Global Search feature (“Gloda”.) Check out this article about it:

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/global-search

A few of points it mentions...

- Gloda returns searches for each work separately. It disregards punctuation, which is why the dot in your search terms are ignored.

- You can enclose a phrase in quote marks and it will search for it as a phrase. I find that this works, but not consistently.

- It only indexes terms of three or more characters, which is why "bt" is ignored.

You can also use the Search Messages feature, found in the menu item <Edit | Find | Search Messages...> or Ctrl-Shift-F to create more specific and detailed queries. It's pretty accurate. Its limitation is that only works on a single folder (plus subfolders) at a time.

There's also the Quick Filter:

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/quick-filter-toolbar

BACKUP

RESTORE

  1. ensure thunderbird is installed, run once, and NOT running
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. delete the thunderbird folder
  4. you should be in Appdata\roaming folder , copy&paste the exported Thunderbird folder there.
  5. start thunderbird and all should be there

content:
Some background info.... IMAP is designed to show whatever is on server. That's how it works. Gmail stores everything in the 'All Mail' folder. Gmail understands that is unworkable when trying to organise and view emails. Gmail invented 'Labels' which work like a type of tag. The benefit means it's easier to organise emails and in addition, possible to apply more than one label to one email. Email therefore can be seen in two Labels eg: Inbox and Important. Gmail created a bunch of default Labels eg: Inbox, Sent etc It means it's easier to find anything that has come in and anything that has been sent etc. Gmail does not have an Archives folder as such - Archive to gmail means remove all labels and store in 'All Mail'. So it's not exactly easy to work out what has been stored - but in 'All Mail' those emails will not have any labels shown.

Any email you send using the gmail smtp server is auto saved in the default server Sent folder. Gmail do this by default just in case you viewed via the gmail webmail account.

It's generally considered not worth seeing 'All Mail' in Imap because it just duplicates everything. I'd also advise you do not allow to show in imap because if anything happens to it - eg: your Anti-Virus attempts to fix it, there is a good chance you lose everything. If email is not in 'All Mail' then it cannot display in any imap folder as it will not exist on server. The risk is just not worth it.

Thunderbird has no concept of 'labels', so it has folders and just downloads whatever is in server eg: Inbox to imap Inbox.

re :Re: the other folders, I hid them from view in Gmail (3rd and 4th screenshots attached - You have selected to not allow Thunderbird to access specific server default labels by not selecting 'Show in imap'. Some I agree it's not worth it, but 'Sent' is definitely one you should select. The 'Show in label list' only applies to the webmail view and not Thunderbird imap account. The 'Show in Imap' effects what Thunderbird gmail account is allowed to see - subscribed to see. Currently, gmails server 'Sent' label has checkbox 'Show in Imap' as not selected. However, for any email you send using the gmail account in Thunderbird, gmail should have copies in the gmail default 'Sent' folder anyway.

Advise: in gmail webmail - for the default 'Sent' - select that 'Show in Imap' so it displays in the imap account. You have no control over Gmail auto saving sent mail, so may as well see what gmail are doing.

In Thunderbird in gmail account: I can see that you are selecting to save sent emails in Local Folders. There is no harm in having a duplicate copy of sent mail stored independently of the server on your computer. But I would advise on altering the set up. In Account Settings > 'Copies & Folders', select 'Place a copy in' use 'Other' and choose 'Sent on Local Folders'. You are already seeing the imap Drafts folder, so I suggest you use it. select 'Drafts folder on' and choose the gmail mail account'

Then make sure the Unified Drafts Folder > Properties > Choose has all 'Draft' folders for all accounts selected and that includes 'Local Folders'

In general, if using an imap folder then select eg: 'Drafts folder on' and select the imap account. if not using a folder specific in the account, then use 'Other' and choose relevant folder in Local Folders.

I'm trying to sort out why you do not have a Unified 'Sent' folder - it's because no default 'Sent' exists which sounds wrong or why 'Sent' folder is not displaying in the very first image you posted under 'Local Folders'.
